restatements.text: Requires every public school classroom to display a poster of the Ten Commandments that is at least 11 by 14 inches in size.

findings.quote: Each public school classroom shall display a poster of the Ten Commandments

findings.quote: Each public school classroom shall display a poster of the Ten Commandments
findings.mechanism: Reduces limits on government endorsement of religion by requiring public institutions to display a specific religious text.

analysis.answer: Currently, there is no law addressing religious displays in public school classrooms. This measure requires that every public school classroom display a poster of the Ten Commandments, specifying a minimum size of 11 by 14 inches.

The direct cost includes the acquisition, printing, framing, and installation of posters for every public school classroom in the state. Because the mandate is highly likely to face constitutional challenges, there are also likely to be significant legal and administrative costs for the state or local districts defending the requirement in court.

Public school districts and the state will bear the financial and legal costs of implementing and defending the mandate. Individuals and organizations who wish to see the Ten Commandments promoted in public schools benefit.

Civil rights organizations, advocacy groups, or parents are highly likely to sue to block the law, arguing it violates the Establishment Clause of the First Amendment. In response to the unfunded requirement, districts may seek private donations to supply the posters.
The measure addresses the absence of the Ten Commandments in public school classrooms by legally mandating their display.
